title: Prove exact lattice closure for rational rounded shears (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. For rational nonintegral a,b and half-up rounding R, the opposite rounded shears preserve a common proper full-rank additive sublattice of Z^2 exactly when a*b is an integer. On every such lattice, both increments are already exact.

```text
L = {(h*n, r*n+k*m)}, g=gcd(r,k), ell=h*k/g
U_a(L)=L iff k=1 or a*h/k is an integer
V_b(L)=L iff ell=1 or b*g/ell is an integer

both slopes nonintegral:
proper common L exists iff a*b is an integer
positive witness for a=p/q: L=q*Z x |p|*Z
```

In particular, slopes 1/2 and -4/5 admit no proper common invariant integer lattice. This excludes one fixed additive lattice as a precision domain surviving each rounded substep of that rational planar lifting pair. It does not exclude changing domains between stages or closure only after a completed word.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit woklerx / PR1848 for the explicit intervening-update closure question and affine-lattice precision interface, and Gareth Davidson, Chafik Boukhalfa and Ali Romman for the retained precision/dirty-restoration lineage. Adam Gall / PR1908 already gives a different actual-leaf closure counterexample. Their results are cited, not rechecked. Hermite normal form and floor-increment methods are classical; no literature-wide priority claim is made.

## Evidence

Before: PR1848 leaves actual update closure open. After: PROOF.md supplies an exact criterion for this separately rounded planar model and the all-rational existence equivalence.

Local CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

- 75 Hermite lattices and 39 reduced slopes give 5,850 closure comparisons against 664,950 literal point updates over complete residue periods. The finite-period reduction has a separate written proof.
- All 784 ordered nonintegral-slope pairs are checked. The 56 integer-product pairs have explicit positive lattice replays with 40,800 additional point updates. The other 728 pairs have no proper invariant lattice in the bounded family; the universal exclusion rests on the written proof.
- Ten semantic controls and ten invalid-input rejections pass. Warning-strict normal and optimized commands pass, timed locally at 0.5001 and 0.5202 seconds, below their 120-second limits. These are replay-budget timings, not speedup claims.
- Registered metadata/pin validation and both commands pass. In-memory syntax/function-length inspection, staged whitespace, all six committed file bytes and declared source ancestry pass. The checker generates a JSON stdout receipt bound to all six package hashes; no receipt is handwritten.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem requires one full-rank additive integer lattice, fixed rational slopes, half-up rounding and exact addition after separately rounding the increment. Both nonintegrality hypotheses are essential for the product equivalence. Affine cosets, lower-rank or nonlinear domains, changing stage domains and completed-word-only closure are outside scope.

Actual selected-caller reachability, physical native implementation, precision/movement/storage prices and the complete paid/productive invoice remain open. No supplier admission, new kappa, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. All five framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, predecessor scientific suites, Lean, Docker, independent human review and formal proof-kernel review are unrun or unclaimed. Every registered command ran locally; no declared check is deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

Can changing lattice domains support one actual rounded lifting caller? First derive its exact image domain at every literal substep, then establish the later inverse-domain compatibility and full precision/movement/storage bill. The common-lattice obstruction does not settle that question. Investigation stops at this first proved result.

## Related open work

- [PR6438](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6438) constructs unbiased periodic reversible rounding for the same cosine-3/5 planar phase. It changes the stochastic whole-map contract; this result concerns deterministic rounded-shear substep closure and computes no competing error optimum.
- [PR4017](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4017) supplies a source-bound reversible native macro on a finite Gaussian lattice. This theorem concerns common full-rank additive domains in the unbounded integer plane and computes no native macro cost or source-specific error.
- [PR6429](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6429) bounds temporary integer widths in rational rounded gates. This result decides lattice closure and computes no temporary-width bound.
